title: Length of an instruction gate list
statement: Let $\kappa$ be a finite type, let $m,w,n$ be natural numbers, let $F$ assign to each $a\in\kappa$ a function from Boolean lists to Boolean lists, and let $z$ be a Boolean list. Let $T$ be the maximum over $a\in\kappa$ of the total size of the fixed circuit representations of the $w$ output coordinates of $F(a,\cdot)$, counting one output gate for each coordinate, and set $W=m+T+w$. For every natural number $i$ and every instruction over $\kappa$, the gate list constructed for that instruction has length $W$.
hypotheses_covered: A function $F$ from each kind to a function on Boolean lists
caveat: The theorem’s width uses a particular circuit construction for each output coordinate; the payload defines that construction formally but does not provide an independent informal description of it.
